subject: Biology
chapter: Chapter 17: Breathing and Exchange of Gases
central_question: How does the human respiratory system move air, exchange gases and transport oxygen and carbon dioxide to support cellular metabolism?
in_scope_units: Respiratory organs and the human respiratory system.
Exchange of gases at alveoli and tissues.
Transport of oxygen and carbon dioxide in blood.
Neural and chemical regulation of respiration.
banned_topics: Plant Krebs cycle and respiratory quotient

known_pitfalls.claim: The lungs actively pull air inward.
known_pitfalls.correction: Respiratory muscles enlarge the thorax, lowering intrapulmonary pressure so atmospheric pressure drives air in.

known_pitfalls.claim: Most CO2 is carried bound to haemoglobin.
known_pitfalls.correction: About 70 percent is transported as bicarbonate; 20-25 percent as carbaminohaemoglobin.

known_pitfalls.claim: Oxygen is the main normal regulator of breathing.
known_pitfalls.correction: CO2 and H+ are the more important chemical signals under normal conditions.
